title: XTendRMT RMT Document
description: Machine-readable schema for XTendRMT Template (RMT) documents.

x-xtendrmt.jsonFallbackPolicy: .rmt.json and .json remain supported for edge-case hosts that cannot serve custom MIME types, but new XTendRMT documents should use .rmt.

templateAuthoringModels.kernelBoundary: XTend component references remain adapter data and must not become RMT kernel imports.

rootLifecycleModels.kernelBoundary: RMT scheduler plans root phases through endpoint hints; host adapters execute framework-specific lifecycle work.

hostCapabilityModels.negotiation: RMT documents may require or prefer capability IDs, but the XTend Host Adapter resolves and executes them.
hostCapabilityModels.kernelBoundary: RMT kernel negotiates host capability data only and must not import XTend runtime modules.

scaffoldCompatibilityBindings.boundary: Scaffold compatibility bindings are dry-run metadata and must not implement the XTendRMT bridge.

templatePilotFlowModels.kernelBoundary: Template pilot flows are reference records; host adapters inspect and materialize XTend component attachments outside the RMT kernel.

hostAdapterLifecycleContracts.kernelBoundary: RMT kernel may register adapter records and schedule abstract lifecycle operations, but host adapters execute framework-specific work. XTend, XRouter and xstate stay outside kernel imports.

adapterRegistryContracts.kernelBoundary: RMT kernel may compare adapter records and capability requests, but framework-specific fallback, manifest lookup, router setup and state writes stay in adapters.
adapterRegistryContracts.templateOnlyCompatibility: Documents without adapter requirements remain valid and negotiate to an empty or implicit-compatible request set.

nativeDomainContracts.backwardCompatibility: Template-only documents without adapters remain valid because adapters is optional and not part of required.
nativeDomainContracts.kernelBoundary: Adapter records are declarative. RMT kernel may parse and negotiate them, but runtime imports, manifest lookup, router setup and state writes stay in adapters.

nativeDomainContracts.backwardCompatibility: Template-only documents without components remain valid because components is optional and not part of required.
nativeDomainContracts.kernelBoundary: Component records are declarative. RMT kernel may parse, normalize and schedule them, but XTend manifest lookup, Custom Element registration, DOM materialization and hydration stay in adapters.

nativeDomainContracts.backwardCompatibility: Template-only documents without routes remain valid because routes is optional and not part of required.
nativeDomainContracts.kernelBoundary: Route records are declarative. RMT kernel may parse, normalize and schedule them, but XRouter imports, x-route DOM generation, navigation side effects and URL state writes stay in router adapters.

nativeDomainContracts.backwardCompatibility: Template-only documents without schedules remain valid because schedules is optional and schedule refs still accept string or inline policy hints.
nativeDomainContracts.kernelBoundary: Schedule records are declarative. RMT kernel may parse, normalize and compare policies, but endpoint execution, DOM work, router side effects and host scheduling stay in adapters or scheduler endpoints.

nativeDomainContracts.backwardCompatibility: Component records with metadata.surface remain valid. During handoff, native surfaces records may coexist with component metadata and must preserve component, route, schedule and state keys.
nativeDomainContracts.kernelBoundary: Surface records are declarative. RMT may parse, normalize and index them, but WindowManager execution, DOM materialization, xstate writes and Fabric diagnostics stay in the xtend.surface adapter and XTend components.

surfaceAdapterContracts.componentCompatibility: components[*].metadata.surface remains the migration source until productive adapter rollout.
surfaceAdapterContracts.kernelBoundary: The xtend.surface adapter consumes normalized surface records and may call the SurfaceController, but the RMT kernel never imports XTend components, DOM APIs, xstate or Fabric.

dslNormalizationContracts.backwardCompatibility: Template-only documents normalize with empty native domains, no required adapters/components/routes/schedules and templateOnlyCompatible=true.
dslNormalizationContracts.kernelBoundary: DSL normalization may build reference graphs and diagnostics, but adapter execution, router registration, component mounting, DOM work and xstate writes stay outside the RMT kernel.

adapterConsumption: router adapters consume routeRegistry.byRouter and routeRegistry.byPath
component adapters consume componentRegistry.byAdapter and componentRegistry.byTag
scheduler bridges consume scheduleRef on route and component entries
runtimeRegistryContracts.kernelBoundary: Runtime registries may index normalized records, expose lifecycle intents and emit missing route/component diagnostics, but route navigation, component mounting, DOM work, XTend, XRouter and xstate execution stay in adapters.

navigationSync: XRouter routechange -> legacy route model detail
xrouterAdapterContracts.kernelBoundary: The XRouter adapter consumes runtime registry snapshots and may register XRouter routes or navigate through an XRouter target, but the RMT kernel only sees adapter operations and never imports XRouter, DOM APIs or xstate.

mountHydrationModel: Custom Element registration is checked by the adapter
props and attributes are applied by the adapter
slots and event bridges are attached by the adapter
hydration sets data-xtend-hydrated and may call element.hydrate
xtendComponentAdapterContracts.kernelBoundary: The XTend component adapter consumes component registry snapshots and may create, mount or hydrate Custom Elements through a host target, but the RMT kernel only sees adapter operations and never imports XTend components, the XTend manifest, Custom Elements, DOM APIs or xstate.

stateSchedulerDiagnosticsBridgeContracts.kernelBoundary: The State/Scheduler/Diagnostics bridge consumes adapter results and schedule refs, may mirror state to an optional xstate target and may call host scheduler endpoints, but the RMT kernel never imports xstate, XTend, XRouter, diagnostics hubs or performance runtimes.

artifactParityContracts.buildPolicy: Upstream RMT source remains the source-of-truth; xtendrmt/ artifacts are synchronized regression references in this repository. RKSH-WP-10 keeps the Trust/Panic/Recovery hardening layer in schema, manifest, types and runtime artifacts.
artifactParityContracts.kernelBoundary: Artifact parity checks drift only and must not introduce XTend, XRouter, xstate or DOM runtime imports into the RMT kernel.

upstreamHandoff.kernelBoundary: RMT kernel remains host-neutral and must not import XTend, XRouter or xstate runtime modules.
